subject: Provisional uptime baseline & monthly remedy scaling for CloudForge deal
messages:
From: Alex Reyes <alex.reyes@cloudforge.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 27 Jul 2027 12:12:00 -0700
Subject: SLA baseline question for CF integration

Hi Naomi / Marissa,

Thanks again for yesterday's demo — the throughput looked promising. Procurement asked me to confirm the SLA template we discussed. Two asks from their side:

1) Given our heavy batched inference pattern (large prefix reuse, cold-cache at start of day), can Redwood accept a provisional uptime baseline of 99.5% for the first 90 days post-cutover rather than 99.9%? We expect request patterns to stabilize over time.
2) On monthly remedies: procurement prefers a simple pro-rata credit rather than the stepped band approach in the template — they want a formula we can present to finance.

If you can propose language that covers a temporary baseline and a clear monthly credit calculation (and any caps), that would help speed approvals.

Attached: CF's standard PO template (for context).

Appreciate it —
Alex

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: SLA baseline question for CF integration

Alex — thanks for the clear note and the PO. Quick technical context that informs our recommendation:

- Batched inference with large prefix reuse can produce higher apparent latency/availability variability during the initial warm-up window because KV cache population and JITed kernel paths reach steady state only after sustained request patterns.
- For customers doing heavy nightly batches or large morning ramps, we typically see an initial ~4-6 week stabilization where observed availability is slightly lower per naive edge checks even though end-user impact is minimal once caches warm.

Suggested commercial approach (to balance your finance team's simplicity ask and our reliability commitments):

1) Provisional baseline: 99.5% uptime for the first 90 days post-cutover, automatic step-up to 99.9% after a one-time health review if observed metrics show steady-state behavior.

2) Monthly remedy formula (simple, auditable):
   - Define monthly uptime U (percent measured at per-service route level).
   - Credit = monthly_invoice_amount * min(0.20, max(0, (0.999 - U) / 0.001 * 0.10))
     * Explanation: If uptime drops below 99.9%, the formula prorates up to a 10% credit per 0.1% shortfall, capped at 20% monthly invoice. This keeps calculations transparent and caps exposure.

3) Operational buffer: During the 90-day provisional window, Redwood will provide a monthly check-in (shared dashboard link) and a single remediation credit cap exception request route for incidents tied to deployment/configuration changes (not platform availability).

I've attached a short analysis and a sample credit-calculator (spreadsheet) so procurement can see the math with example invoices. Laura, looping you for any minimal legal tweaks to wording for the Master Services Agreement.

If that looks acceptable to CloudForge, Marissa and I can roll the language into the SOW and DocuSign packet.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Reyes <alex.reyes@cloudforge.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 Jul 2027 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA baseline question for CF integration

Alex — thanks Naomi for the write-up. Commercially, here's the proposal I'll put into the SOW if you agree:

- Term: Standard 12-month term starting on production cutover.
- Uptime baseline: 99.5% for first 90 days post-cutover (provisional). Automatic review on day 91; upon mutual confirmation of steady-state metrics, baseline moves to 99.9%.
- Monthly Remedy: Use Naomi's formula. I'll translate into plain language in the SOW: "If measured monthly uptime U is below 99.9%, Customer will receive a pro-rata credit calculated as (monthly invoice) * P where P is proportional to the percentage shortfall, with a maximum credit equal to 20% of the monthly invoice."
- Exceptions: Platform maintenance windows and customer-initiated configuration changes are excluded.
- Governance: Monthly sync for the first 3 months (15-minute ops check) plus a 30-day post-cutover health review.

Example calculation (from attached spreadsheet):
- Monthly invoice: $120,000.
- Observed uptime: 99.55% (U = 0.9955). Shortfall from 99.9% = 0.35% => formula yields credit approx $4,200 (3.5% of invoice * pro-rata factor in calculator).

If that reads OK, I'll prepare the SOW language and a DocuSign packet. Laura, please flag any legal language that needs to be tightened around "automatic review" and "operational buffer".

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
